caveats: **The fast open is more permissive than the walk in two ancestor-only cases.** An ancestor the caller may traverse but not read: the walk answers `access_denied`, the fast open accepts. An ordinary non-link ancestor that carries a value named `SymbolicLinkValue`: the link probe cannot tell it from a link, so the walk answers `key_is_link` and the fast open accepts. In both the write lands on the real requested key, which is what registry 1.0.0's single open did; probing every ancestor on the fast path would cost it the constant call count. A decoy value on the LEAF is refused on both paths. A path whose case differs from the stored one only outside ASCII, `HKCU`, `HKCR`, a missing key and any failed name query take the walk (same verdicts, more calls); if the kernel name of `HKLM` or `HKU` cannot be read at the first write, the fast open is off for that root until the agent restarts.

**The audit trail is lossy by design.** Key and value names go through `yuzu::log_token` (space, `=`, `,`, control bytes and `|` become `_`; over 256 bytes they are cut with `~<length>`) and old/new data is hex capped at 256 raw bytes, so an audit row identifies the change but cannot always reproduce it (there is no digest of a value cut at 256 bytes, and a `delete_key` row carries counts, not values: `old=-|new=-`); `old=` and the delete counts are point in time, so a stale `old=` can make a restore overwrite a concurrent writer; the response row carries the exact value; the single actions accept a value named `-`, whose audit line renders `name=-` exactly like the default value. Rows exist only for agents that stamp `CommandResponse.action`: an agent at v0.14.1 or earlier writes registry values but produces no `registry.write` rows, and a read action never does. An exception inside a mutating action answers a bare `error|exception` (rc 1) with no audit line; the server's `command.dispatch` row and the stored response keep the attempt attributable to the command.

**Behaviour changes from 1.0.** The changes to existing actions are listed in the 2.0.0 changelog entry (`changelog.d/2026-10-22-registry-typed-writes.changed.md`) and in `docs/user-manual/upgrading.md`, which also gives the rollout order (server replicas first) and the minimum agent version for `registry.write` rows (the first release that contains the audit binding of #6294, later than 0.14.1). **Mixed fleets:** an agent still running registry 1.x writes an EMPTY `REG_SZ` over the value for a `data_hex`-only `set_value` (it reads only `name`, `value` and `type`), stores `REG_QWORD`, `REG_MULTI_SZ`, `REG_EXPAND_SZ` and `REG_BINARY` values as `REG_SZ` text, reports `status|ok` for all of those, and follows a write under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet` that 2.0.0 refuses; nothing on the server gates dispatch on a plugin version (the definitions' `minAgentVersion` is stored and shown, not compared), so upgrade the agents before using the new types or `data_hex`.

**`delete_key` removes only a key with no subkeys.** A key with subkeys is refused `key_has_subkeys` and nothing is deleted; there is no recursive delete and no `dry_run` in this version (the `dry_run` column is always 0). The key's own values go with it, and the counts are a point-in-time read of them.

**The read-side gaps are unchanged.** `enumerate_values` writes `value|<name>|<type>` (the leading `value` is a literal tag, not a third column), `get_value`/`enumerate_values` leave `REG_MULTI_SZ`/`REG_LINK` values hex-encoded where `get_user_value` decodes them (changing that changes `get_value`'s output for existing callers), and `PrivilegeScope`'s `AdjustTokenPrivileges` call must keep its `ReturnLength` argument (without it the offline fallback silently never enabled the privileges until #2771: `agents/shared/win_profiles.hpp`, `changelog.d/2771-privilegescope-token-adjust-bug.fixed.md`). The `get_user_value` capture exercised the live-hive path, not the offline mount.

definitions.description: Delete a Windows registry key that has no subkeys; a key with subkeys is refused as key_has_subkeys and nothing is deleted. The key is opened on a checked handle (one canonical-name-checked open, with a component walk as the fallback) and a registry symbolic link in the path is refused, never followed (the key AT the path may itself be a link: the link object is removed and its target is untouched). The delete runs by handle on the checked key (no RegDeleteTreeW, which follows links) and is confirmed by the handle reading back as deleted. counted_keys is 1 and counted_values is the number of values the key held; the value count stops at 10,000, past which capped is 1 and counted_values is a lower bound (the delete still removes the key with all its values). Windows-only.

Delete a specific value from a Windows registry key; the key itself is left in place. Registry 2.0.0 reports a failure as an `error|<token>` line (key_not_found, value_not_found, key_is_link, access_denied ...) instead of a sentence, limits the key path to 255 bytes and 32 components, and emits one leading `audit|op=delete_value|...` row (the old value, hex) before `status|ok`. Windows-only.
List all immediate subkeys under a registry key, one row per subkey. Windows-only.
List all value names and types under a Windows registry key, one row per value. Value data itself is not returned — use get_value to read a specific value. Windows-only.

Read a registry value from a specific user's registry hive. Resolves the target profile via ProfileList (by username or an explicit SID), then reads the live HKEY_USERS\<SID> hive if the user is logged in, or loads that profile's NTUSER.DAT via RegLoadKey as a fallback. SeBackupPrivilege and SeRestorePrivilege are required only for the offline fallback when the target user is not logged in; reading an already-loaded live hive needs no elevated privilege. Windows-only.

Read a value from the Windows registry. Value data is decoded for REG_SZ/REG_EXPAND_SZ/REG_DWORD/REG_QWORD; every other type, including REG_MULTI_SZ and REG_LINK, is returned as hex-encoded bytes rather than decoded (get_user_value decodes both of those). Windows-only.
Check whether a registry key exists, without reading any of its values. Windows-only.

Enumerate local Windows user profiles from HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList: SID, resolved profile name, profile path, and whether the profile's registry hive is currently loaded under HKEY_USERS. System profiles (LocalSystem, LocalService, NetworkService) are excluded. Windows-only.

Write a value to the Windows registry, creating missing key components beneath an existing top-level key (a path whose first component is missing is refused as root_level_create). All six writable types are supported (REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ, REG_BINARY, REG_DWORD, REG_MULTI_SZ, REG_QWORD) and the write is verified: the previous value is captured first, the new one is read back on the same handle and compared byte for byte, and a mismatch fails the action. The key is opened on a checked handle (one canonical-name-checked open, with a component walk as the fallback) and a registry symbolic link anywhere in the path is refused, never followed; a write under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet, itself a link, therefore fails as key_is_link. The previous and new values are recorded in a `registry.write` audit row (hex, capped at 256 bytes). Windows-only.

description: Windows Registry -- get, set (six types, verified), delete value, delete key, enumerate, per-user reads
how_it_works:
All nine actions are direct, synchronous Win32 registry calls: there is no scheduled gather. The six read actions (`get_value`, `key_exists`, `enumerate_keys`, `enumerate_values`, `get_user_value`, `list_profiles`) open a key read-only and read or list it; every registry-controlled string they render passes through `sanitize_field` (`|`, CR and LF become `_`), so no read output can contain a line that starts with `audit|`. `get_user_value` resolves the target profile through the same `ProfileList` walk `list_profiles` exposes, reads the live `HKEY_USERS\<SID>` hive if the user is logged in, and falls back to an offline `RegLoadKeyW` mount of `NTUSER.DAT` (under `SeBackup`/`SeRestore` and a process-wide mutex serialising the whole offline arm) only when the user is logged out. The seven `hive`+`key` actions validate through one `parse_target` helper, which also logs (never blocks) access to a few sensitive `HKLM` subtrees via `spdlog::info`.

The three mutating actions (`set_value`, `delete_value`, `delete_key`) share one core (`registry_core.hpp`, over an injected registry; `registry_win.cpp` binds it to `Reg*W`). Each obtains a CHECKED handle for the key, and every step after that -- the previous-value capture, `RegSetValueExW`, the verifying read-back, `RegDeleteValueW`, `NtDeleteKey(h)` -- runs on that handle: nothing re-resolves the path by name, and no handle outlives the command. There are two ways to the handle.

- **The fast open (`HKLM` and `HKU` only).** ONE `RegOpenKeyExW` of the whole path with `REG_OPTION_OPEN_LINK`, then `NtQueryKey(KeyNameInformation)` names the object the handle is bound to. The open is accepted only when that kernel name equals `<root kernel name>\<requested path>` (every byte exact except that A-Z fold, so a name that differs in non-ASCII case, a name that does not fit the 4 KiB buffer and a failed query all decline) and the leaf has no `SymbolicLinkValue`. A registry link before the leaf makes the kernel open the link's TARGET, whose name cannot equal the requested one, so the fast open can only accept the canonical object with no real link traversed; everything else declines to the walk. A `set_value` on an existing key is 7 calls across the plugin's registry seam (`open_path`, `final_name`, the link probe, capture, set, read-back, close; the cached root-name lookup is an eighth), the same at every depth; they are about 9 Win32 calls, because the capture and the read-back are each a size call and a data call. The walk costs about 3 more per path component.
- **The walk (the reference).** `open_checked` walks the path component by component from the hive root, opening each component from the previous HANDLE with `REG_OPTION_OPEN_LINK` and probing it for `SymbolicLinkValue`: a registry link is refused (`key_is_link`), never followed. It is always used for `HKCU` (it resolves per calling user) and `HKCR` (a merged view of two trees), neither of which has one kernel name to compare with, for a key that is missing, and whenever the fast open declines. It alone produces the verdict token and creates: a missing component is created component-wise from the checked parent, a create that finds the key already there refuses `concurrent_change`, and a creating action never creates a key directly beneath the hive root (`root_level_create`).

The two differ in exactly two ancestor-only cases where the walk is the stricter (see Caveats); in both the write lands on the real requested key, as registry 1.0.0's single open did. A path under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet`, itself a link to the active control set, is refused on both: write under `HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001` (or the numbered set `Select\Current` names); registry 1.0.0 followed it, reads still do. `set_value` writes any of the six types (`REG_SZ`, `REG_EXPAND_SZ`, `REG_BINARY`, `REG_DWORD`, `REG_MULTI_SZ`, `REG_QWORD`) from text or exact `data_hex` bytes, reads the value back on the same handle and compares type and bytes; a mismatch fails the action (`verify_mismatch`). `delete_key` refuses a key that has subkeys (`key_has_subkeys`) and otherwise deletes the key by handle with `NtDeleteKey`, never `RegDeleteTreeW`, which follows a registry link met inside a tree; a link at the leaf is opened as the link object, so the delete removes the link and never its target. Its counts are what the key held: `counted_keys|1` and `counted_values|<n>`, with `capped|1` when the value enumeration stopped at its 10,000-value cap (`counted_values` is then a lower bound; the delete still removes the key with all its values). Every mutating action captures the previous value first and emits ONE `audit|` line (see "Audit line grammar and producer contract").

Code anchors (file and function; line numbers move with every edit): the fast open `open_fast`, the checked walk `open_checked` and its link probe `probe_link`, the guarded value read `query_value_bounded`, the verifying write `write_value_on`, the by-handle delete `delete_key_on` and the counts in `delete_key_tree` (all in `registry_core.hpp`); the encoders `encode_value`, `validate_key_path` and `render_audit_line` (`registry_parsers.hpp`); the kernel calls `Win32Registry::open_path`, `final_name`, `root_name` and `delete_key_by_handle` (`registry_win.cpp`); the server-side binding `registry_audit_events_for_frame` (`server/core/src/plugin_result_audit.hpp`).

outputs_note: This plugin does not emit a uniform pipe-joined "row"; each action has its own shape. `get_value`, `get_user_value` and `key_exists` write one self-describing `field_name|value` line per field on success; a failure writes an `error|...` line and returns rc 1, so `-` is never used as an absence placeholder in the read actions. Every mutating action that resolves its target writes ONE `audit|...` line first (grammar below; `-` is "not applicable" inside it), then `status|ok` or `error|<token>`; a missing hive or key or an unparseable hive is a bare `error|...` line with nothing opened and no audit line, while a key path or value name that fails shape validation after the hive resolved is audited as `result=refused`; the dashboard shows the `audit` line as one more row. `delete_key` appends four `key|value` rows after `status|ok`: `counted_keys` (1), `counted_values` (the values the key held), `dry_run` (always 0 in this version) and `capped` (1 when the value count stopped at the 10,000-value cap, which makes `counted_values` a lower bound; the key is still deleted with all its values); the counts are point in time, since a writer racing the delete can add values the count never saw. `enumerate_keys` writes one `subkey|<name>` line per subkey; a genuinely empty key emits zero lines with rc 0. `enumerate_values` writes one line per value shaped `value|<name>|<type>` -- the leading `value` is a fixed literal tag, not one of the two documented columns (`name`, `type`); see Caveats. `list_profiles` writes one true pipe-joined row per profile (`<sid>|<name>|<path>|<state>`, no discriminator prefix) and zero rows is a structural success.

privileges.grant: Writes against `HKLM\*` need the service account in `Administrators`; `HKCU\*` needs no elevation. `get_user_value` uses the offline-hive fallback only when the target user is logged out: it needs `SeBackupPrivilege`+`SeRestorePrivilege`, already granted to the service account, so there is no new grant; the live-hive path, the machine-hive writes and `list_profiles` need no elevated privilege beyond the key's own ACL. `NtDeleteKey` and `NtQueryKey` (ntdll) need no privilege beyond `DELETE` on the key and a handle the caller already holds.
privileges.if_refused: `error|key not found` / `error|value not found` (reads); the mutating actions name the cause: `error|access_denied`, `key_not_found`, `value_not_found`, `key_is_link`, `key_has_subkeys`, `concurrent_change`, `root_level_create`, `verify_mismatch`, `invalid_key_path`, `invalid_value_name`, `invalid_type`, `invalid_data`, `value_overflow` or `win32:<code>`

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Rows/lines travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore (90 days), queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`.

**Audit log.** The server records a `registry.write` row only for a `registry` command whose agent-stamped `CommandResponse.action` is one of the three mutating actions; an agent older than this plugin stamps none and produces no rows. Principal, result, retention and the join to the operator's row: `docs/user-manual/audit-log.md`.

**Not consumed by** daily-sync inventory, the TAR warehouse, DEX, or metrics: nothing here runs on a schedule; the plugin executes only when an operator or workflow dispatches one of its nine definitions.

**Sensitivity.** The audit rows and the `set_value`/`delete_value` responses carry registry data OLD and NEW (hex of the raw bytes, 256 bytes at most per value in an audit row) and key paths, so they can hold secrets that live in the registry (a service account's autologon password, a product key, an agent token). `get_value`/`enumerate_values`/`get_user_value` can return arbitrary registry data, among it `RegisteredOwner`/`DigitalProductId` (a person's name and a device-specific product-key hash); `get_user_value`'s `username` and `list_profiles`' `profile_name`/`profile_path` (e.g. `jsmith`/`C:\Users\jsmith`) directly identify a person and their home directory. The readers are wider than the writers: `AuditLog:Read` and `Response:Read` (the Operator, PlatformEngineer and ITServiceOwner roles hold both; `Response:Read` is not floored while RBAC is off), the legacy `/events` stream (any authenticated session) and MCP `query_audit_log`; the write parameters (`value`, `data_hex`) are stored unredacted in `executions.parameter_values`, and `delete_value` returns the old value in its response too. Read-time redaction is not built.
**Siblings:** none. Guardian's own real-time registry-key watch (`guard_type: "registry"`) is an unrelated detection mechanism; this plugin is on-demand only, with no watch/trigger surface.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) -> `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) -> `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("windows.registry.get_value")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`; the audit rows: the audit log API filtered on `registry.write`.
